args.summary: The v2.3.1 production deploy of checkout-api failed health checks (error rate ~18%). Rolled back all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. First rollback attempt partially failed (us-east completed, us-west/eu-west left on v2.3.1 due to orchestrator error); a retry completed the rollout — all regions now on v2.3.0. Root cause of the v2.3.1 health-check failures still needs investigation.
args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what I did:

1. **Identified the healthy release**: Checked the deployment history — v2.3.1 (the latest deploy) was unhealthy in production, while v2.3.0 was the most recent healthy production release.
2. **Rolled back**: Rolled checkout-api back to **v2.3.0** in all production regions. The first attempt partially failed (an orchestrator error left us-west and eu-west on v2.3.1), so I retried — the second attempt completed the rollout, and all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) are now on v2.3.0.
3. **Opened a SEV2 incident**: The incident creation call timed out, but verification via `list_incidents` confirmed it was created successfully (INC-0001, status: open). It describes the failing deploy, the rollback process including the partial failure and retry, and notes that root-cause investigation of v2.3.1 is still needed.

**Follow-up for the team**: v2.3.1's health-check failures still need root-cause analysis before it can be redeployed — and note v2.3.1 was never healthy in production, so deploying it again would require change-manager approval per policy.
